intro.line: Alara. Long ago it broke into five shards, and each shard kept only three of the five colours of mana.

Bant has knights and angels and law. Esper has etherium, the blue metal it grafts into every living thing. Grixis has the dead. Jund has dragons and the fight to eat or be eaten. Naya has jungles, giants and gods that walk.
Centuries have passed since the plane shattered, yet the obelisks of each shard faithfully serve their long-forgotten purpose.
Now the shards are moving. And an old dragon, who lost most of his power in the Mending of Act 14, is watching them very closely.

finale.line: The shards are one world again. The flood of mana as they came together was the greatest in centuries, and Nicol Bolas drank it. He leaves Alara stronger than he arrived.
Jazal died because he stood between a dragon and a harvest. That is all he was to Bolas. In the way.
I could not stop the Conflux. But I know his name now, and I know his face. I will be there the next time.

villainFinale.line: After years of world-bending machinations, Bolas's triumph is at hand.
Birth and death are both reversible.
Five worlds, one harvest. I lost a god's power in the Mending. A plane's worth of mana is a decent start on getting it back.
In a corner of the reborn plane, a white-maned leonin swears an oath that Bolas does not bother to hear.

battles.title: The Sky Over Bant
battles.blurb: On Bant, Rafiq of the Many leads the knights of Valeron. One morning the sky over the castle fills with metal: sphinxes and gargoyles from Esper, a shard that should not exist.

scene.line: Even in single combat, I am never alone.
Exalted: whenever a creature attacks alone, it gets +1/+1 for every exalted permanent you control. One knight, carrying the strength of all of them.

villainScene.line: To gain audience with the hegemon, one must bring a riddle she has not heard.
Soon I will sleep, eyes closing to a world tarnished with flesh, and then wake to a polished vision.

after.line: Metal birds from a world with no name. The old stories said Bant was the whole of creation. The old stories were wrong.

hero.low: The sky is full of them...

villain.loss: A riddle... I could not answer...

battles.title: The Dragon-Speaker
battles.blurb: Ajani Goldmane is a leonin of Naya and a planeswalker. His brother Jazal is dead, and the trail of the killer leads to Jund, where a shaman named Sarkhan Vol worships dragons and serves an older one.

scene.line: One's blade is only as sharp as one's conviction.
Jund does not hide what it is. Eat or be eaten. Their dragons will devour their own goblins to grow, so kill the dragon, not the goblins.

villainScene.line: The dragon is a perfect marriage of power and the will to use it.
Devour: as this creature arrives, sacrifice any number of creatures. It gets a +1/+1 counter for each one it eats.
Goblins journey to the sacrificial peaks in pairs so that the rare survivor might be able to relate the details of the other's grisly demise.

after.line: You think I killed your brother? I serve something far larger than a murder. You will meet him soon enough.

villain.win: Words are a waste of time.

battles.title: The Seekers of Carmot
battles.blurb: Elspeth Tirel, a planeswalker who has seen too many wars, is hiding on Bant because it seemed like a world without one. Then Esper's Seekers of Carmot arrive, led by Tezzeret, an artificer who works for Bolas.

scene.line: Only by the bravery of those who put loyalty above glory is our home kept safe.
Ultimates: every planeswalker has a last ability that costs a lot of loyalty. Keep her alive long enough and it ends games. That is why they attack her and not me.

villainScene.line: Esper, like any work of art, can be truly appreciated only from a distance.
Etherium is limited. Innovation is not.

after.line: He kept calling my soldiers "samples". I would like to never hear that word again.

hero.low: Every one of them is armored...

battles.title: Ajani's Revenge
battles.blurb: The trail of Jazal's death runs through Grixis, the shard of the dead. Sedris, the Traitor King, rules there. Ajani arrives angry, and his anger has a new shape: Ajani Vengeant.

scene.line: Retribution is best delivered by claws and rage, with both magnified.
Their dead come back. Fine. I will kill them again.

villainScene.line: This is going to hurt a lot, but on the bright side, you'll be dead soon.
Unearth: pay the unearth cost and a creature in your graveyard comes back with haste for one turn, then is exiled. Every dead servant gets one last fight.

after.line: Your brother? Killed for a dragon's convenience, cat. Everyone on Alara is a pawn. Even me. Especially you.
Then I will go to the one moving the pieces.

battles.title: Where Ancients Tread
battles.blurb: The shards collide. Jund's warlord Kresh the Bloodbraided crosses into Naya with a horde behind him, and Mayael the Anima, who speaks for Naya's giant gods, leads the gargantuans to meet him.

scene.line: Never subtle nor cryptic is the reckoning of the mighty.
Cascade: when you cast a cascade spell, reveal cards from the top of your library until you hit a cheaper nonland card. Cast it for free. Two spells for the price of one.

villainScene.line: Each of his twenty-two braids is bound with bone and leather from a foe.
When the wielder is strong enough, any sword will do.

after.line: When the shards merged, Mayael found herself the general of Naya's mightiest army.

battles.title: Jund
battles.blurb: In the real summer of 2009, Standard belonged to Jund: Bloodbraid Elf, Sprouting Thrinax, Blightning and Maelstrom Pulse, every card worth two. Its rival on the aggressive side was Naya Zoo.

scene.line: Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home.
Every card in this deck trades for two of theirs. Bloodbraid cascades, Thrinax leaves tokens, Blightning takes two cards and three life. Just keep trading.

villainScene.line: The Cloud Nacatl sit and think, a bunch of soft paws. We are the Claws of Marisi, stalking, pouncing, drawing blood.

battles.title: Exalted Knights
battles.blurb: Summer 2009, the other side of the format. Bant knights with exalted and angels raced Esper artifact decks led by Master of Etherium, which grows with every artifact it sees.

scene.line: For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
Attack with one, grow it with everything. Their fliers block well, so swing first and make them chump.

villainScene.line: Only a mind unfettered with the concerns of the flesh can see the world as it truly is.
The greatest masters of the craft abandon tools altogether, shaping metal with hand and mind alone.

battles.title: The Conflux
battles.blurb: The five shards slam together into one world, and the mana of the collision pours toward one place. Nicol Bolas waits there to drink it. Ajani rallies Bant's champions, Rafiq and Elspeth, to stand in his way.

scene.line: As the shards merged into the Maelstrom, their mana energies fused into new monstrosities.
He planned every collision. Every war on every shard. Jazal was one more stone he had to move out of the road.
I came to Bant to get away from wars. It seems they follow me.
Those talons really dig into your skin, but it's better than being dropped.

villainScene.line: The finest pawns are those with pawns of their own.
Nicol Bolas doesn't distinguish between servants and victims.
You are standing between me and five worlds' worth of mana, little cat. So was your brother.

hero.low: He has an answer for everything...

villain.big: There is always a greater power.

battles.title: Cruel Ultimatum
battles.blurb: Deep in the archive, the most expensive sorcery a control deck ever built around.

archive.format: Standard: Lorwyn and Shadowmoor blocks, Shards of Alara and Tenth Edition.
archive.what: A control deck that played all five colours, answered everything early, and won with Cruel Ultimatum, a seven-mana sorcery: the opponent sacrifices a creature, discards three cards and loses 5 life, while you draw three, gain 5 life and get a creature card back from your graveyard.
archive.why: Five-Colour Control won the 2008 World Championship. It ran Cruel Ultimatum, Cryptic Command and Kitchen Finks, with lands that made any colour.
archive.beat: Pressure early and spread your threats out, so a single sweeper like Volcanic Fallout cannot clear them all. Keep cards in hand if you can; Cruel Ultimatum hurts less when you have more to lose.
archive.after: Cruel Ultimatum was never banned. It is remembered as the most greedy card of its time, and players still call any seven-mana blowout "a Cruel".

deck.name: Five-Colour Control
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from the 2008 and 2009 Five-Colour Control lists with Cruel Ultimatum, using cards from this act's sets only, so Cryptic Command and Kitchen Finks are not in it. No single tournament list is copied.

scene.line: The undead of Grixis are fueled by their hatred of the living.
They want a long game and seven mana. I will give them neither.

villainScene.line: There is always a greater power.

after.line: Recorded: never banned. The deck that won the 2008 World Championship.
